title: Harness requirements
description: Formal shape of harness-requirements.yaml — the properties the methodology requires of the harness that hosts it, each stated as observable behaviour with its observation point and the evidence that admitted it (COR-047). Adapters answer these in their own support declarations; a requirement with no declaration, or whose observation point a check cannot reach, resolves indeterminate. Companion per COR-018 / the .pkit/schemas/ area conventions.

requirements.description: Entries. Keys are kebab-case ids; values match $defs.entry.

entry.description: One harness requirement (COR-047). Stated as behaviour any harness could satisfy — never as one harness's key, flag, or tool.

behaviour.description: The observable behaviour the methodology depends on, in harness-neutral terms (COR-047 point 1).

observation_point.description: Where the requirement's truth is visible (COR-047 point 4): out-of-session — configuration, environment, versions, platform; interposed-runtime — code the harness runs at its own hook points, which sees calls but not schemas; in-session — only an agent holding the harness's own view of its tools. A verification pass that cannot reach this point resolves indeterminate.

evidence.description: The demonstrated defect or concrete design dependency that admitted the requirement (COR-047 point 9).

retirement_condition.description: For a requirement that exists because of a transient defect in a foreign tool: the condition under which it retires (COR-047 point 9).
